latin_text: Raphaelem coelestem medicum advocemus, qui nos morali et dialectica uti pharmacis salutaribus liberet. Tum ad valetudinem bonam restitutos iam Dei robur Gabriel inhabitabit, qui nos per naturae ducens miracula, ubique Dei virtutem potestatemque indicans, tandem sacerdoti summo Michaeli nos tradet, qui sub stipendiis philosophiae emeritos theologiae sacerdotio quasi corona preciosi lapidis insignet.
english_translation: let us call upon Raphael, the heavenly physician, to set us free with moral philosophy and dialectics, as if with healing drugs. Then, once we have been restored to health, Gabriel, the strength of God, will abide in us and, leading us through the marvels of nature and showing us everywhere the merit and the power of God, he will finally deliver us to Michael the high priest, who will in turn bestow upon us, who will have completed our service to philosophy, the insignia of theological priesthood, as if a crown of precious stones.
exegesis:
[VERIFIED] Pico concludes his entire argument by invoking the three great Archangels as the guides and enablers of human transformation. Raphael (*Healing of God*) is the celestial physician who administers *pharmacis salutaribus* (healing drugs): moral philosophy (*philosophia moralis*) and dialectic (*dialectica*). These two disciplines heal the soul's ethical corruption and restore rational order. Gabriel (*Strength of God*, also rendered as *God is my strength*) then leads the recovering soul through *natura miracula* (*the marvels of nature*), revealing everywhere *Dei virtutem potestatemque* (the power and might of God). This is natural philosophy proper: understanding creation as the theophany through which God reveals himself. Finally, Michael (*He who is like God*, the great warrior-prince of Kabbalistic theology) receives the soul who has *emeritos...philosophiae stipendiis* (completed its service to philosophy) and bestows upon it *theologiae sacerdotio quasi corona preciosi lapidis insignet* (the insignia of theological priesthood like a crown of precious stones).

The philosophical function is to provide the complete map of the ascent from moral healing through natural knowledge to theological consecration. [VERIFIED] These three archangels correspond to the three domains of human knowledge and practice: ethics (Raphael), physics (Gabriel), theology (Michael). But the language emphasizes mediation: each archangel *facilitates* the passage; the archangels are not merely exemplars but active agents in human transformation. They represent divine powers actively working to restore and elevate human nature. The phrase *quasi corona preciosi lapidis insignet* (like a crown of precious stones) invokes the Urim and Thummim (the breastplate of the High Priest) and suggests that the consummated soul becomes a bearer of divine light, a precious stone set in the cosmic order.

[INFERRED] The three-fold division—Raphael/ethics-logic, Gabriel/natural philosophy, Michael/theology—parallels the threefold division of the Heptaplus (literal, allegorical, anagogical on the ethical level; allegorical, tropological, anagogical on the natural level; anagogical, Kabbalistic, neoplatonic on the mystical level). It also parallels the Commento's four-fold structure: Book I (foundation in ethical restoration), Books II-III (natural and cosmological mysteries), Book IV (mystical union and theological perfection). Being & Unity grounds this entire ascent metaphysically: Raphael restores participated ethical being, Gabriel elevates participated natural being, Michael perfects participated theological-mystical being.
notes: The three archangels function as guides through the philosophical ascent. Raphael (medicine/moral healing) → Gabriel (natural miracles/knowledge) → Michael (theological priesthood). This is the complete ladder of angelic mediation into human transformation.
